The study (acsnano-7b02404) says the V2O5 film was held under elastic prestrains of <2% imposed on the V2O5[1]. The largest strain actually measured on the film was:

- **Out of plane (along the 'c' axis):** a compressive strain of 0.5%[2], measured by XRD. The text describes this compressive strain as (<1%)[3].
- **In plane:** the matching tensile strain, estimated using a Poisson ratio of v = 0.3[4], was 1.6%[5]. Elsewhere the paper puts this maximum at ∼1.66% in-plane prestrain[6]. At this strain the paper reports its measured shift in intercalation potential and its largest gain in lithium diffusion (Fig. 5[7]).

These film strains are much smaller than the strain applied to the NiTi wire underneath, which was stretched by 0−10%[8]. The DFT simulations went further than the experiments, modelling in-plane prestrain on the V2O5 lattice up to ±2%[9].
